input: Write a Yelp review for my favorite local bookshop

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which specific aspects of the shop to cover (selection, staff, ambiance, events, etc.) determines what the review focuses on and whether it feels complete.
Understanding who the review is meant to persuade (book lovers, casual browsers, families, tourists) shapes the angle and what details to highlight.
The name and type of the bookshop (independent, used books, niche genre focus) anchors the review in specifics that make it credible and useful.
Yelp reviews vary from a few sentences to several paragraphs; knowing the desired length ensures the output fits what the user wants to post.
Tone — warm and personal vs. informative and straightforward vs. witty and fun — greatly changes how the review reads and whether it sounds like the user.
Knowing whether the goal is to boost the shop's visibility, share a personal story, or warn about something specific defines what a 'great' review actually looks like.
Whether the user wants a ready-to-paste draft or a flexible template to personalize determines how finished and specific the output needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Write a Yelp review for local bookshop
gold.taskDescription: Write a compelling Yelp review for the user's favorite local bookshop that accurately reflects their experience and opinion.

questions.title: What is the name and type of this bookshop?
questions.description: Ask for the shop's name and a brief description (e.g., independent general bookstore, used books only, genre-focused like sci-fi or mystery) so the review is grounded in real, specific details.

questions.title: Which specific aspects of the shop do you most want to highlight?
questions.description: Ask the user which features matter most to them — e.g., curated selection, knowledgeable staff, cozy atmosphere, events, prices, a cafe — to determine the core focus of the review.

questions.title: Is there a particular experience or visit you want to reference?
questions.description: Find out if there is a specific memorable moment or story from the shop that should anchor the review and make it feel authentic and personal.

questions.title: How long should the review be?
questions.description: Establish the desired length — a short punchy blurb (2-3 sentences), a medium review (1-2 paragraphs), or a detailed long-form piece — so the output fits Yelp norms and the user's intent.

questions.title: What tone should the review have?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants the review to feel warm and personal, witty and playful, or informative and straightforward, so the writing style matches their voice.

questions.title: What is the main thing you want a reader to walk away thinking?
questions.description: Identify the single strongest impression the review should leave — e.g., 'this is a hidden gem,' 'the staff are exceptional,' 'perfect for book lovers of all kinds' — to define success.

questions.title: Do you want a ready-to-post draft or an editable template?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a fully polished, specific review they can copy and paste directly, or a flexible draft with placeholders they can personalize before posting.
